topic: What if you fell off a cruise ship in the middle of the ocean

through_line.name: the orange lifebuoy ring
through_line.progression: decoration on the railing, then thrown over, then far off and blinking, then reached and hugged, then held up as a beacon
through_line.resolution: back on its bracket in daylight, the passenger safely behind the railing it came from

locations.deck_night: top deck of a cruise ship at night, railing with a mounted lifebuoy ring
locations.fall_air: midair beside the towering white hull at night, water far below
locations.underwater: below the surface at night, bubbles rising into deep blue-black
locations.diagram_stage: clean chart stage with a human body outline and a big thermometer
locations.ocean_night: black ocean surface at night, receding ship lights on the horizon
locations.ship_stern: the cruise ship seen from water level behind, wake churning white
locations.bridge: ship bridge interior with the wheel, radar screen and wide windows
locations.warm_sea: turquoise tropical daylight sea surface with a low sun
locations.cold_sea: grey fog-bound northern sea surface with cold swells
locations.lifeboat_sea: an orange rescue lifeboat on the daylight sea, binoculars on the bow
locations.deck_day: the same cruise ship railing in bright daylight, sea beyond

blocks.vo_line: Forty meters of air, then the ocean. That is the drop from a cruise ship's top deck at twenty knots at night.
blocks.through_line_state: mounted on the railing beside the passenger
shots: WIDE establishing: the passenger leans on the night railing as the deck rolls, the lifebuoy ring mounted beside them
CU low angle: the passenger's sandal slides on the wet deck plank and lifts
MEDIUM lateral: the passenger tips over the rail, arms flailing, ring left behind
ECU high angle: the ring's orange curve fills frame as the figure drops past it
WIDE high angle looking down: the figure shrinks toward the black water far below

blocks.vo_line: Roughly two dozen people go over the side of cruise ships every year, and only about one in five is pulled out alive.
blocks.through_line_state: still mounted on the rail as the deck empties
shots: MEDIUM lateral: five cutout passengers pop up in a row along the railing, staggered
CU: four of the five figures flip to grey one after another, one stays colored
WIDE high angle: the deck, now empty, the mounted ring the only orange left
ECU: a checkmark and four crosses stamp down beside the ring
MEDIUM low angle: the surviving colored passenger raises a hand as the others fade

blocks.vo_line: The fall lasts under three seconds, about thirteen floors, and you hit the water at close to ninety kilometers an hour.
blocks.through_line_state: a shrinking orange dot on the deck above
shots: WIDE establishing: the passenger falls beside the hull, thirteen deck rows sliding upward
ECU: a speedometer dial needle sweeps hard to the right and shudders
MEDIUM: the falling passenger tumbles past lit portholes, the ring a dot above
CU: wind rips at the passenger's shirt, eyes squeezed shut
WIDE low angle from the water: the figure drops straight toward camera

blocks.vo_line: At that speed water feels like pavement, so go in feet first with your legs together, arms crossed and chin tucked down.
blocks.through_line_state: far above on the rail as the water rushes up
shots: MEDIUM: the passenger snaps from a starfish sprawl into a straight pencil shape
ECU: arms fold across the chest and the chin drops, one snap
WIDE lateral: the pencil figure plunges past the hull, feet pointing down
CU low angle: a red cross stamps over a belly-first splayed silhouette
MEDIUM high angle: the pencil figure hits the surface in a tight white splash

blocks.vo_line: You plunge four or five meters into darkness, your ears pop, and every nerve in your body is screaming one word: up.
blocks.through_line_state: a blurred orange glow far above the surface
shots: WIDE: the passenger sinks in a column of bubbles, the surface a pale sheet overhead
ECU: the passenger's ear with a sharp pop ring drawn around it
MEDIUM low angle: the passenger kicks, hair streaming, looking up
CU: the passenger's eyes open wide in the dark
WIDE high angle: a single bold arrow drops in pointing up, the ring glowing faintly above

blocks.vo_line: Then the real danger begins, because cold water forces an involuntary gasp, and if your face is under, that gasp is seawater.
blocks.through_line_state: drawn as a small orange circle at the diagram's edge
shots: MEDIUM: the body outline on the chart stage fills with cold blue from the feet upward
ECU: the mouth of the outline snaps open and a big gasp bubble bursts out
WIDE lateral: a water line slides up across the outline until it covers the face
CU: water pours into the open mouth of the outline, lungs flash red
MEDIUM low angle: the passenger, small at the stage edge, claps both hands over their mouth

blocks.vo_line: Survival experts have a rule for this, and its first number is sixty seconds spent doing nothing but slowing your breath.
blocks.through_line_state: on the ship's rail, lights shrinking on the horizon
shots: WIDE establishing: the passenger floats on their back on the black swell, ship lights far off
CU: the passenger's chest rises and falls, breath clouds slowing
ECU: a stopwatch face with a single hand sweeping one full turn
MEDIUM high angle: the passenger's legs drift up level with the surface
CU lateral: the passenger's eyes close and the mouth settles into a calm line

blocks.vo_line: Meanwhile the ship is not stopping, because a hundred thousand tons moving at twenty knots needs well over a kilometer to halt.
blocks.through_line_state: mounted on the stern rail, pulling away
shots: WIDE establishing: the stern towers over the water, wake boiling white, the passenger a speck
ECU: a giant anchor icon swings but the hull keeps sliding past it
MEDIUM low angle: the passenger bobs as the wake rolls over them
CU: the stern rail with its mounted ring slides out of frame right
WIDE high angle: a long dotted line draws from the ship far ahead back to the passenger

blocks.vo_line: That works out to ten meters every second, so one minute of catching your breath leaves the ship six football fields away.
blocks.through_line_state: a speck of orange on the receding stern
shots: MEDIUM: six football field cutouts stamp down end to end across the water, staggered
ECU: a ticking counter of dots fills one by one
WIDE lateral: the ship now tiny at the far end of the fields, the passenger at the near end
CU low angle: the passenger squints at the distant lights
MEDIUM high angle: the last field drops in with a thud and the ship slips beyond it

blocks.vo_line: Worse, nobody may have seen you fall, since hull sensors that trigger an overboard alarm are still missing from many ships.
blocks.through_line_state: still hanging on the empty rail, unnoticed
shots: MEDIUM: the empty night deck, deck chairs, nobody at the rail, the ring hanging idle
ECU: a hull sensor grid glows red then flickers out to grey
CU high angle: a question mark stamps beside the dark sensor
WIDE lateral: a row of five hulls, three carry glowing grids, two stay dark
MEDIUM low angle: the ring on the rail swings gently, nobody near

blocks.vo_line: Suppose a passenger saw you, so the bridge gets the call and a lifebuoy flies over the rail trailing light and smoke.
blocks.through_line_state: thrown over the rail, trailing light and smoke
shots: CU: a crew member's hand slams a red alarm button
MEDIUM lateral: the crew member yanks the ring off its bracket and hurls it over the rail
ECU: the ring's strobe light blinks on as it clears the rail
WIDE high angle: the ring falls trailing orange smoke toward the black water
MEDIUM low angle: the crew member points down over the rail, other arm waving

blocks.vo_line: That ring is not thrown for you, it marks the exact spot you went in, a fixed point on a very blank ocean.
blocks.through_line_state: floating far off, strobe blinking, marking the spot
shots: WIDE: the ring bobs alone on the black swell, strobe pulsing, smoke drifting
ECU: the strobe flash blooms across the water
MEDIUM high angle: a pushpin stamps down onto the ring's position, the passenger far away
CU lateral: the passenger turns their head toward the distant blink
WIDE high angle: a dotted circle draws itself around the ring on an otherwise empty sea

blocks.vo_line: On the bridge the captain swings the wheel one way then the other, a Williamson turn looping the ship back onto its wake.
blocks.through_line_state: its strobe a dot on the radar screen
shots: WIDE establishing: the bridge, a crew member at the wheel, the radar screen glowing with one dot
CU: hands spin the wheel hard to one side, spokes blurring
ECU: the radar dot for the ring pulses at the screen's edge
MEDIUM lateral: hands spin the wheel back the other way, the crew member leaning
WIDE high angle overhead: a ship icon traces a looping path back onto its own dotted wake

blocks.vo_line: For a vessel this size that maneuver takes ten to fifteen minutes, and you are a coconut floating in a parking lot.
blocks.through_line_state: a faint blink on the swell, still far
shots: ECU: a clock face with the hand sweeping through a quarter turn
WIDE high angle: the passenger's head, tiny, on a vast flat grey-black expanse
MEDIUM: a coconut drops in beside the passenger's head, same size, bobbing
CU low angle: the passenger glances at the coconut, deadpan
WIDE lateral: the ring's blink far off, the passenger and coconut drifting

blocks.vo_line: Remember the rule, its second number is ten minutes, roughly how long cold water leaves your arms and legs able to work.
blocks.through_line_state: drawn orange at the stage edge, closer than before
shots: MEDIUM: the body outline on the stage, arms and legs glowing red
ECU: a ten-tick dial fills tick by tick
CU lateral: the outline's arms fade from red to blue, fingers curling
WIDE high angle: the whole outline goes blue from the limbs inward, torso last
MEDIUM low angle: the passenger at the stage edge shakes out stiff arms, ring behind them

blocks.vo_line: Spend them wisely, kick off heavy shoes, yet keep a light jacket on, because it traps a warm layer against your skin.
blocks.through_line_state: blinking ahead, nearer with each swell
shots: CU: the passenger's shoes slip off their feet and sink, one then the other
MEDIUM lateral: the passenger zips the light jacket up to the chin
ECU: a thin glowing layer of warmth traced between jacket and skin
WIDE high angle: the passenger paddles toward the blinking ring, closer now
MEDIUM: a checkmark stamps beside the jacket, a cross beside the sinking shoes

blocks.vo_line: Then swim for that lifebuoy if it landed anywhere near you, because that orange ring is now your entire world.
blocks.through_line_state: reached at last, both arms hooked through it
shots: MEDIUM low angle: the passenger's hand stretches and grabs the ring's edge
ECU: fingers lock around the orange foam, strobe flashing against the knuckles
WIDE lateral: the passenger hauls their chest up onto the ring on the black swell
CU: the passenger presses their cheek to the ring, eyes shut, exhausted
MEDIUM high angle: the passenger and ring float as one shape, everything else dark

blocks.vo_line: Now the water temperature decides everything, since a Caribbean sea near twenty seven degrees lets you float for most of a day.
blocks.through_line_state: hugged to the chest on bright turquoise water
shots: WIDE establishing: bright turquoise sea, the passenger hugging the ring under a low sun
ECU: the thermometer's red column rises high and settles
MEDIUM lateral: a sun arcs across the sky above the drifting passenger
CU high angle: the passenger's sunburnt nose and squinting eyes
WIDE high angle: a day's sun arc drawn over the whole sea, the passenger still afloat

blocks.vo_line: An Alaska cruise or an Atlantic crossing can mean ten degrees, and there the rule's last number, one hour, takes over.
blocks.through_line_state: clutched tight on grey cold water
shots: WIDE establishing: grey fog-bound sea, the passenger gripping the ring in cold swells
ECU: the thermometer's column drops to a low blue stub
MEDIUM: fog rolls over the passenger's shoulders, breath fogging
CU lateral: the passenger's lips turn blue, teeth chattering
ECU: a clock face with one hand, a single full sweep

blocks.vo_line: Cold does not kill you within that hour, it makes you pass out, and then you drown, which is why flotation matters most.
blocks.through_line_state: the only thing keeping the head above water
shots: MEDIUM high angle: the passenger's eyelids droop, head nodding toward the water
CU: the head slumps onto the ring and the ring holds it up
WIDE lateral: a ghost twin of the passenger without a ring slips under the grey surface
ECU: the ring's foam pressing up under the passenger's chin
MEDIUM low angle: a checkmark stamps over the passenger on the ring, a cross over the empty water

blocks.vo_line: Instinct says swim for the ship or the horizon, but swimming drains body heat far faster than lying still and floating.
blocks.through_line_state: drawn beside the floating outline, orange
shots: MEDIUM: two body outlines side by side on the stage, one stroking, one still
ECU: the swimmer's heat bar drains fast, dropping in chunks
CU lateral: the still outline's heat bar drops one slow notch
WIDE high angle: a tiny ship icon far off with a red cross stamped over the path to it
MEDIUM low angle: the passenger at the stage edge lies back onto the ring, arms spread

blocks.vo_line: Instead pull your knees to your chest and hug them, the help position, which shields your armpits, groin and chest from the cold.
blocks.through_line_state: tucked under the curled outline's arms
shots: CU: the outline's knees rise and fold toward the chest
MEDIUM lateral: the outline's arms wrap around the shins, a tight ball
ECU: three warm zones glow orange, armpits, groin, chest
WIDE high angle: the curled outline floats as a compact ball, ring tucked in, blue all around
MEDIUM low angle: the passenger copies the ball shape at the stage edge, nodding

blocks.vo_line: Back at the ship every crew member is on deck with binoculars, and lifeboats drop low enough to spot a head between swells.
blocks.through_line_state: hugged in the water as boats drop nearby
shots: WIDE establishing: an orange lifeboat lowers onto the daylight sea, a crew member on the bow
ECU: the binoculars' twin lenses sweep across the swells
MEDIUM low angle: the crew member braces on the bow, scanning left then right
CU: through the lens rings, a small head on the ring between two waves
WIDE high angle: three lifeboats fan out across the sea, the passenger a dot among swells

blocks.vo_line: Coast guards and nearby ships join in, searching an expanding square pattern that begins at that blinking lifebuoy and grows outward.
blocks.through_line_state: the pushpin center of the search map
shots: WIDE high angle overhead: a flat sea map, the ring as a blinking pushpin at its center
ECU: a boat icon traces the first small square around the pin
MEDIUM: the square path grows outward, a second larger square drawing itself
CU: a second boat icon and a helicopter icon drop onto the map's edge
WIDE lateral: the full expanding spiral of squares, the pin still blinking at the heart

blocks.vo_line: Your job is to be visible, so raise one arm high, wave anything bright, and blow a whistle, since sound carries over water.
blocks.through_line_state: held up high as a bright orange flag
shots: MEDIUM: the passenger thrusts one arm straight up out of the turquoise water and waves
ECU: a cross stamps over a two-armed wave that dunks a ghost twin under
CU low angle: the passenger hoists the orange ring overhead like a flag
WIDE lateral: sound ripples spread from the whistle across the bright sea
ECU: the whistle between the passenger's lips, cheeks puffed

blocks.vo_line: At night that changes, because a searchlight is the only thing that finds you, and the strobe on the ring becomes your beacon.
blocks.through_line_state: a strobe pulsing, the only light in black water
shots: WIDE high angle: near-total dark, one strobe blinking on the black swell
ECU: the strobe flash on the ring lighting the passenger's face in pulses
MEDIUM lateral: a searchlight beam sweeps the water from the left
CU: the beam catches the ring and stops, the passenger squinting into it
WIDE lateral: beam locked on the blinking ring, the sea black everywhere else

blocks.vo_line: And the sharks are statistically not your problem, since open ocean predators rarely bother swimmers, while cold and invisibility do the damage.
blocks.through_line_state: hugged calmly while a shark shrugs past
shots: MEDIUM: a fin cuts the turquoise surface toward the passenger on the ring
CU low angle: the cartoon shark surfaces and shrugs with both fins
WIDE lateral: the shark turns and swims off, the passenger unbothered on the ring
ECU: a red cross stamps over the shark's fin
MEDIUM high angle: a blue cold icon and a blindfold icon stamp beside the passenger instead

blocks.vo_line: People have been found alive after twenty hours in warm water, sometimes by a completely different ship whose lookout spotted them floating.
blocks.through_line_state: clutched as a different ship's bow looms in
shots: ECU: a sun and moon icon swap places twice over the water
WIDE lateral: a different ship's bow appears at the edge of frame, the passenger on the ring below
MEDIUM low angle: a crew member on that bow points down and shouts silently
CU high angle: a rope ladder unrolls down the hull toward the passenger
MEDIUM: the passenger grabs the ladder with one hand, the ring in the other

blocks.vo_line: Here is the twist, cruise railings stand over a meter tall by law, so almost nobody slips, people climb them for a photo.
blocks.through_line_state: back on its bracket in daylight, untouched
shots: WIDE establishing: the same railing in daylight, the ring on its bracket, sea sparkling beyond
ECU: a measuring tape snaps up beside the railing, stopping above the passenger's waist
MEDIUM lateral: the passenger plants one foot on the middle rail and lifts a phone for a selfie
CU low angle: the phone tilts, the passenger's balance wobbles
WIDE high angle: a red cross stamps over the climbing pose, the ring hanging calmly beside it

blocks.vo_line: So float, never swim, and remember the ordeal started on the wrong side of a railing, forty meters of air, one bad decision.
blocks.through_line_state: hanging on the rail, exactly where it belongs
shots: MEDIUM: the passenger steps back down onto the deck, both feet planted
ECU: a green checkmark stamps onto the railing itself
CU lateral: the passenger rests both hands on the top rail, phone pocketed
WIDE high angle: the drop below the rail, forty meters of air to the water, the passenger safely behind it
MEDIUM low angle: the passenger pats the ring on its bracket once and walks off
